explanation: Template specialization allows programmers to define custom implementations of class or function templates for specific types or conditions. This feature is used to optimize or modify behavior for particular data types, enabling more efficient or tailored code while maintaining generic programming capabilities. It is a core aspect of C++ template metaprogramming, facilitating compile-time customization and type-specific optimizations.
example_explanation: This example demonstrates template specialization by defining a general template class 'Calculator' for any type T, with a generic 'compute' method. It then provides a specialized version of 'Calculator' specifically for 'int' types, overriding the 'compute' method with a custom implementation. In 'main', creating instances of 'Calculator<double>' and 'Calculator<int>' shows how the compiler selects the general template for 'double' and the specialized template for 'int'. This illustrates how template specialization enables type-specific behavior while leveraging the flexibility of templates in C++.
